text: Access point periodically broadcasts a packet called beacon. Beacon in English, it's that tower on the coast of the ocean that sends live signals, right? That's the beacon for ships or boats that are along the coast, so that they can see that there is a coast there, right? These packets are called beacons because indeed they announce the fact that there is an access point. So every access point transmits this packet that is intended for anyone. So it's broadcast, it's intended for anyone, and it says, "I'm access point, Mickey Mouse, I'm here." Okay, that's the meaning of the beacon. All the Wi-Fi cards that are nearby can hear the beacon. So when you enter campus, your Wi-Fi card we start scanning. That means you will first position the receiver onto this frequency channel and start listening. If there are beacons from access points, any access point that is there, right? And upon hearing a beacon, your Wi-Fi card understands that there is an access point called Mickey Mouse.
